rules.statement: To establish marriage by habit and repute, evidence of customary rites is not essential if neither party to the marriage is alive and the marriage was contracted at an early date.
rules.supporting_quote: "If one of the parties to the marriage is alive, then of course, it would be necessary to establish the existence of marriage ceremonies, for, a party to the marriage must necessarily be aware of it and be able to give evidence in regard to it; but where neither of the parties is alive, and the marriage itself was contracted at a very early date, evidence of customary rites or religious rites would be difficult, if not impossible, to obtain, and is, therefore, not insisted on. It is for that reason that the law recognises proof of a marriage by habit and repute."
